targets.authors: Gold, J., Tadin, D., Cook, S. C., & Blake, R.
targets.title: The efficiency of biological motion perception.
targets.evidence_quote: We replicated the previous finding of low discrimination efficiency in biological motion (Gold, Tadin, Cook, & Blake, 2008) and also found low detection efficiency for biological motion.
targets.outcome_quote: Note that the ideal thresholds for point lights and silhouette were similar, consistent with the comparable ﬁnding in a discrimination task reported by Gold et al. (2008). However, we found a slightly higher threshold for the point lights than for the silhouette whereas Gold et al. found the same threshold for the two displays. This small discrepancy was likely due to the difference in the number of frames in the walking sequence (we used 10 frames whereas Gold et al. used 20 frames).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Low human efficiency is explicitly confirmed, but the authors also explicitly contrast ideal-observer thresholds with the original. The abstract confirms the particular low-efficiency effect rather than giving an overall verdict over all comparisons; the stated contrast requires mixed under rule 2.

reasoning: Experiment 2 uses newly recruited observers to retest Gold et al. (2008). Other cited ideal-observer studies provide context rather than additional specific targets.
